title: Orchestrated calibration service and golden-suite for Hopper FP8 enablement
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a repeatable, automatable orchestration layer and a compact "golden" evaluation suite that allow safe enablement of FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles on Hopper GPUs across our fleet. Current ad-hoc calibration runs are slow, produce noisy activations, and lack standardized comparison signals for accuracy/regression gating.

Proposal: Build an Orchestrated Calibration Service (OCS) that can schedule deterministic calibration runs per model and per-host, replay recorded micro-batches, and emit a concise set of accuracy and stability signals backed by a curated golden prompt/label suite. The service will drive canary rollouts, store calibration artifacts (scale/clipping stats, per-layer histograms), and provide automatic rollback triggers when drift or accuracy regressions exceed thresholds.

Scope: OCS backend + control-plane hooks, golden prompt suite (200 prompts across categories), calibration replay harness for recorded micro-batches, per-layer drift sentinel, telemetry schema, and a staged canary rollout recipe integrated with the autoscaler and deployment controller.
acceptance_criteria: OCS can execute a deterministic calibration run for a given model and dataset that is reproducible across two independent hosts (bit-identical calibration artifacts at 95%+ of layers)

Golden-suite of 200 prompts produces a stable accuracy baseline; initial activation of E4M3/E5M2 profiles shows <0.5% top-level regression vs float32 (measured by task-specific metrics: exact-match / BLEU / RMSE where applicable)
Per-layer drift sentinel detects sustained mean shift > 3 sigma and triggers an alert within 5 minutes; automated rollback can be initiated by policy
Calibration artifacts (scale factors, clip points, histograms) stored to object store with versioned keys and can be referenced by runtime for fast warm-starting
Canary rollout recipe exists and can move from 1% -> 10% -> 100% across racks with automated gating based on telemetry and SLAs
Telemetry dashboards show token-level latency, tail latency, activation distribution shifts, and quality regressions for canary vs baseline within the Console release page
implementation_notes: Service should be implemented as a small control-plane microservice (Go) that orchestrates workers (Python) for replay runs
Replay harness will accept recorded micro-batches with original KV cache shapes and seed RNG for op determinism where possible
Artifact schema: flat file containing per-layer scale, clip, histogram bucket counts, quant-mode used (E4M3 or E5M2), seed, model commit, and dataset checksum
Integrate with existing rollout engine; add two gating signals: 'quality_regression_rate' and 'drift_sentinel_rate'
Provide a CLI for on-demand local calibration debugging that mirrors OCS APIs
Add unit tests for artifact serialization and end-to-end functional test that runs on a tiny model in CI
telemetry_requirements: Emit 'calibration.run' events with run_id, model, profile, host, duration, result_summary
Emit per-layer summary events at the end of run: mean, std, clip_fraction, histogram_bucket_ids
Create a 'golden_suite_eval' metric set: pass_rate, mean_metric_delta, worst-case-prompt-id
Expose real-time stream to a short-retention canary topic for gating (1h retention, high throughput)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration replay non-determinism across host kernels. Mitigation: record RNG seeds, kernel versions, and optionally restrict canary hosts to validated kernel builds.
Risk: Golden-suite too small -> overfits. Mitigation: curate prompts from diverse tasks (QA, summarization, code, translation) and rotate subset every quarter.
Risk: Storage blowup from artifacts. Mitigation: compress histograms, keep full artifacts for releases only, and use bloom filters for quick membership checks.
Risk: False positives from transient load spikes. Mitigation: require regression to be sustained over 10 minutes and across at least 2 hosts before auto-rollback
notes: Initial spike done by Arjun and Maya produced a prototype that runs deterministic replay for a toy bert-like model (see PR #2489)
Engineering lead review scheduled 2026-03-10: feedback asked to add drift sentinel and compressed artifact format
Plan to onboard two pilot models this quarter: 'chat-small-v2' and 'code-medium-1'
Coordination required with SRE for canary host kernel whitelist and with Storage team for artifact lifecycle policy
